title: Unbounded projection formula for qcqs algebraic-space morphisms
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Use schemes [def-pc-scheme], algebraic spaces with their small etale structure sheaves [def-trf-algebraic-space], module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Z)$ for objects with quasi-coherent cohomology [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Derived pullback and tensor use K-flat resolutions; derived direct image uses K-injective resolutions. Let $S$ be a scheme, let $g:Y\to Z$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$, and let $F\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ and $L\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Z)$. Quasi-compact means that inverse images of quasi-compact spaces are quasi-compact, and quasi-separated means that the diagonal is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. The canonical adjunction-mate projection morphism is an isomorphism in $D(\mathcal O_Z)$: $$(Rg_*F)\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_Z}L\xrightarrow{\sim}Rg_*\left(F\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_Y}Lg^*L\right).$$ The map is adjoint to the tensor pullback of $Rg_*F\otimes^{\mathbf L}L$ followed by the counit $Lg^*Rg_*F\to F$ on the first factor. No flatness, properness, Noetherian or boundedness hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Realize the small etale module functors as ringed-topos functors: the enlarged ringed-site model gives the canonical ringed morphism, and the chart adjunction realization identifies its tensor pullback and direct image with the specified module functors, preserving the units. Work in the equivalent small models in the fixed universes. Apply the ringed projection-mate exactness theorem to $g$. For fixed $F$, put $A(L)=Rg_*F\otimes^{\mathbf L}L$ and $B(L)=Rg_*(F\otimes^{\mathbf L}Lg^*L)$. It supplies the natural transformation $\alpha:A\to B$ whose adjoint is $(\varepsilon_F\otimes1)\mu_{Rg_*F,L}$. This is precisely the morphism in the statement, and is a transformation of exact functors compatible with shifts. Its value at $\mathcal O_Z$ is the identity under the unit identifications.

Choose an etale covering by affine schemes $a:U\to Z$ and set $Y_U=Y\times_ZU$, with projections $b:Y_U\to Y$ and $g_U:Y_U\to U$. Such fibre products and coverings exist by the algebraic-space fibre-product theorem and the affine chart basis of the small model. Quasi-compactness of $g_U$ and of its diagonal follows by base change from $g$ and $\Delta_g$; indeed $\Delta_{g_U}$ is the base change of $\Delta_g$. Thus $g_U$ is qcqs. The chart calculus gives $a^*Rg_*\cong R(g_U)_*b^*$ and $b^*Lg^*\cong Lg_U^*a^*$, with the composition comparisons respecting counits. Together with the tensor pullback comparison these identify $a^*\alpha_L$ with $\alpha^{g_U}_{a^*L}$: both adjoints are the pullback of $(\varepsilon_F\otimes1)\mu$, using the same counit. Exact etale restriction commutes with cohomology. If these restricted maps are isomorphisms, each cohomology map of $\alpha_L$ is an isomorphism on every geometric stalk, since the charts cover all geometric points. Geometric-stalk conservativity then makes each cohomology map an isomorphism, hence $\alpha_L$ an isomorphism in the derived category. It therefore suffices to prove the assertion when $Z=\operatorname{Spec}R$. The restrictions of $F,L$ remain quasi-coherent by the chart calculus.

Now assume $Z=\operatorname{Spec}R$. Let $\mathcal T$ be the full subcategory of $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Z)$ consisting of $L$ for which $\alpha_L$ is invertible. The affine etale realization $a_R:D(R)\simeq D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Z)$ is the termwise exact associated-module functor, and takes $R[k]$ to $\mathcal O_Z[k]$. On the affine scheme, the perfect-localizing-generation theorem ensures that the quasi-coherent derived subcategory is closed under ambient coproducts and distinguished-triangle cones. We will check that $\mathcal T$ contains these shifted units and is closed under those operations and retracts.

For a small family $(L_i)$ in $\mathcal T$, derived pullback and tensor preserve coproducts: pullback is a left adjoint by the derived adjunction in the projection-mate theorem, and tensor in either variable is a left adjoint by the closed symmetric monoidal theorem. Apply the left-adjoint colimit theorem to the corresponding small discrete diagrams. Each $F\otimes^{\mathbf L}Lg^*L_i$ has quasi-coherent cohomology by the quasi-coherent pullback/tensor theorem. The qcqs derived pushforward coproduct theorem therefore applies to this family. Consequently both $A$ and $B$ preserve its coproduct. Naturality for every injection $L_i\to\bigoplus_iL_i$ identifies $\alpha_{\bigoplus_iL_i}$ with $\bigoplus_i\alpha_{L_i}$ under these comparisons, by the coproduct universal property. The latter has inverse $\bigoplus_i\alpha_{L_i}^{-1}$, so $\bigoplus_iL_i\in\mathcal T$.

For a distinguished triangle with vertices in $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Z)$, the exactness and shift compatibility of $\alpha$ established in step 1 make its three components a morphism of distinguished triangles. The triangle two-out-of-three theorem shows that if two vertices are in $\mathcal T$ then so is the third. The same shift compatibility, iterated forwards or backwards, shows that $\mathcal T$ is closed under every integer shift. In particular all $\mathcal O_Z[k]$ belong to it, because $\alpha_{\mathcal O_Z}$ is the identity by step 1.

The class $\mathcal T$ is closed under isomorphisms by naturality. For a retract $i:L\to M$, $p:M\to L$ with $pi=1_L$ and $M\in\mathcal T$, an inverse to $\alpha_L$ is $A(p)\alpha_M^{-1}B(i)$. Naturality gives $\alpha_LA(p)=B(p)\alpha_M$ and $B(i)\alpha_L=\alpha_MA(i)$, so composing in either order gives respectively $B(pi)=1$ and $A(pi)=1$. Thus $L\in\mathcal T$.

Transport $\mathcal T$ along the affine equivalence $a_R$. An equivalence preserves coproducts by their universal property; here these are ambient coproducts by step 3. Since $a_R$ comes from the termwise exact associated-module functor, it also carries shifts and distinguished triangles to shifts and distinguished triangles. Thus the transported class in $D(R)$ contains every $R[k]$ and is closed under small coproducts, triangle two-out-of-three and retracts, by steps 4--6. Derived-module free generation implies that it is all of $D(R)$. Essential surjectivity of $a_R$ now gives $\mathcal T=D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Z)$. This proves the formula for affine $Z$; step 2 proves it on every $Z$. The construction throughout is the canonical mate from step 1, without any boundedness or flatness restriction.
